correctness.rationale: The Steiner-normalized V3 is the three-segment wedge sum. A three-edge forest contributes 2sqrt2 (disjoint edges), sqrt6 (two-edge path plus isolated edge), or 2 (a connected four-vertex tree), while a triangle contributes zero. Multilinear inclusion-exclusion over deleted edges gives ((binom(n,2)/3)-k)A_n+binom(k,2)B_d-Delta_n P(D)-U(D); adjacent/disjoint prescribed pairs have the stated B_a,B_d. The exact inequality Delta_n>2sqrt2(k-2) for n>=2k follows from the displayed successive differences and n=4,6 bases, and bounds each nonmatching deleted-edge adjacency incidence in triple weights; similarly disjoint deleted-edge pairs imply the star minimum. Pairwise-intersecting deleted edges are a star or a triangle, with the latter strictly larger. Independent direct incidence Gram determinants and full enumeration of every deletion pattern for 4<=n<=7 and admissible k verified the identity and relabeling-unique extrema; finite enumeration is only corroboration.
